note:
One record per PHOTOGRAPH, and every record is a licence statement waiting to be true. NOTHING HERE IS A REGULATION: a record says what an image shows, who took it, where it came from and on what terms it may be used, and it never says what may be taken.

THE FOUR LICENCE STATES, AND WHY THERE ARE FOUR AND NOT THREE.
`pending` — the request has gone out and nobody has answered. 35 records are pending today and they are NOAA Fisheries' illustrations: NOAA offered one licence agreement covering all 35 on 2026-09-22 and it is not signed. A pending record has no file, no sha256 and no pixel size, and the app draws a neutral placeholder card that says 'Illustration requested from NOAA Fisheries; not yet licensed.' Nothing about a pending record may be bundled, cached or previewed — not the image, not a thumbnail of it. The 160 Macaulay records were pending from 2026-09-19 until 2026-09-22, when the Library answered; they are `declined` now, and what that means is three paragraphs down.
`candidate` — an image somebody CHOSE and whose licence was read once, by the research lane, on a day that is written down. It is not permission and it is not a claim: it is a shortlist entry carrying everything `fetch-public` needs to re-read the licence for itself. A candidate has no file either. Twelve records were candidates on 2026-09-19 and none is today: all twelve are now `licensed`.
`licensed` — the licence has been re-read by the pipeline, at the source, and quoted verbatim with its URL. Only a licensed record may carry a file, and the build refuses a licensed record that carries no statement.
`declined` — the answer was no, or the licence could not be read at all. The record STAYS, with the reason quoted, because a species whose photograph was refused keeps its card and its sentence: silently dropping it would leave a reader thinking this app simply has no opinion about a bird it was refused a picture of. 160 records are declined today: every photograph this project asked the Macaulay Library, Cornell Lab of Ornithology for. On 2026-09-22 the Library answered the ticket filed on 2026-09-19, and the answer is quoted on all 160 records the way this project quotes a regulation — "Unfortunately at this time, Macaulay Library media is not authorized for use within any outside mobile applications. We also don't have staff to handle commercial licensing right now and are focused on educational and research requests." — with the thread, the message, the sender and the date it arrived beside it. The reason on all 160 is `source_policy_excludes_mobile_apps`, which was added to the vocabulary that day because nothing already in it was true: the refusal is a policy about the KIND of use, not a licence term, and it excludes a free build of this app exactly as firmly as a paid one. The 46 birds keep their cards, their names and their scientific names, and each card now says 'Photo declined by Macaulay Library, Cornell Lab of Ornithology; none will be shown.' Nothing about a declined record may be bundled, cached or previewed either — the Debug preview hook is `pending`-only for this reason. `expired` is declared for the day a term runs out and is unused today.

`trait` is what makes a photograph an IDENTIFICATION photograph rather than decoration, and it is never this project's opinion of an image it has not seen. For the Macaulay records it is the trait this project ASKED FOR, verbatim from the request CSV beside this file. For the twelve public-domain images it is the Commons file title the research lane recorded, and `trait_review` is `pending` until a person looks at the contact sheet and replaces it with the marks the frame actually shows (the California Quail is the first to be `approved`, by `fable` on 2026-09-19, and carries `trait_reviewed_by` and `trait_reviewed_on` to say so) — which is also why `sex_age` is null on all twelve even where the title says 'drake' or 'buck'.

`credit_line` is null until a licence says what it must say. It is never composed from a photographer's name by this project's own guess: getting a required credit wrong is a breach of the licence that granted the image.
THE SECOND READ, AND HOW ELEVEN OF THESE TWELVE CAME TO BE LICENSED. This contract makes a read at the image's ORIGINAL source mandatory and will not accept the Wikimedia Commons register entry alone. On 2026-09-19 `fetch-public` licensed one of the twelve and declined eleven `source_licence_unreadable`: their original source pages are on www.flickr.com, whose robots.txt refuses `User-agent: *` outright, so the command could not make that read. The scrape policy's own words for a disallowed host are "manual/phone lane only", and that lane is now built: `curated/species_media_manual_source_reads_2026.json` holds, per image, the licence line the page printed, the label on the licence link, the deed URL that link points at, the owner as the page names them, and who read it, when and how. `fetch-public --retry-declined` re-opened the eleven, took each manual read as the source-side statement, put it through the same accept/reject table and the same divergence check against Commons, and licensed all eleven on 2026-09-19. Every one of them records `license.source_read: "manual"` with the reader and the date beside it, because a licence read by a person is evidence only while you can say who, when and how — and a read here stands for 180 days, after which the record falls back to `declined` and somebody opens the page again.

media.trait: A PAIR of adult Gambel's Quail facing each other on a mud wall against a plain blue sky, both birds whole and in profile. LEFT BIRD = HEN: plain grey-brown head with NO black face mask and NO chestnut crown, a short black teardrop plume, grey-brown breast and back, a plain buff belly with NO black patch, and chestnut-and-white streaked flanks. RIGHT BIRD = DRAKE: black face bordered white, chestnut crown, black belly patch, same streaked flanks. Both birds are the same species, so the frame teaches the hen and the sex difference in one picture. No person in frame.
